how: Members ask for help creating the mark and direct helpers to the main organising chat.
A creator retrospectively identifies the small group that wanted its own mark and welcomed others who built and repaired it.
Members propose and reject visual changes using design preferences and the need to direct viewers to the correct subreddit.
The creator reports others creating and fixing the dog retrospectively rather than supplying a continuous construction log.
Members circulate a heart guide and doggo blueprints as shared instructions.

statement: Moving decisions into chat and returning instructions
how: A main organising chat receives planning and border discussion, making the venue move an additional process beyond circulating templates.
Participants report hardcoded design features and warn users to stop automated placement with stale coordinates.
Stopping stale coordinate targets is a necessary finer step when automated placement preserves an unwanted version.
A text-change vote places this room on the claim's explicitly decided-order side without testing its cross-room frequency.
Repeated polls establish an attempted procedure for choosing the room's future without revealing the outcome.
Participants report sustained defence, request reinforcements and recall repairing a repeatedly reverting pixel.
Maintenance includes rejecting a contributor's unapproved feature, so repair must be described relative to the version being maintained.
A border dispute is corrected when construction is distinguished from destruction and an interlocutor admits misreading commands.
Participants negotiate Dutch borders and accept a clog-wearing dog plan while continuing to express differing accounts of the conflict.
A moderator restrains expansion to avoid invading allies and taking unfair space from other artworks.
Participants request neighbours' help, offer to reclaim a letter and propose reciprocal labour for another character.
A protection bargain, shared heart design and later ally acknowledgement support the minimal joint-work form of coalition.
A participant permits the disputed anatomical addition if the rest is protected and receives explicit assent.
Personal permission counts as a room commitment only with a recognised mandate, which the speaker explicitly disclaims.
A bare agreement accepts a conditional proposal without requesting anything further.
Questioned about speaking for the subreddit, the person offering terms explicitly limits the agreement to personal opinion.
A reported protection-for-design bargain supports partial accommodation under a stronger neighbour without establishing comprehensive territorial command.
An interlocutor brings Dutch border demands and reports misunderstood leader commands, while the record leaves formal authorisation unresolved.
The warning that bots will kill a proposed addition expresses a judgement that the desired extra work cannot hold there.
The principal dogs are reported surviving, so relocation is unnecessary to explain their ending while the failed small dogs remain a separate loss.
A named Dutch opponent does not establish a pre-canvas quarrel for a subreddit confirmed as created for the dog.
Character recognition in a canvas-born subreddit cannot establish a pre-existing collective identity without a pre-event record.
The attack call supplies a national target but no explanation connecting that target to an evidenced prior tie.

statement: A canvas mark gathering its own community
how: The visible mark recruits a defender and a subscriber into the community formed around it, adding a return from the canvas to room formation.
A moderator confirms that the subreddit was made for the canvas dog, supporting the dedicated-venue form of boundary work.
Creating a venue around an existing canvas mark must be distinguished from an older host containing excessive canvas talk.
Recognising the character through jokes does not evidence an April Fools takeover or a room-specific licence for fake claims.
Participants celebrate survival and thank the strangers who came together to help.
Creators recount their wish to leave a mark and distinguish the dog they made from earlier versions.
Farewells mark the end and place the dogs in the platform's history.
A pixel-perfect claim is qualified by recollection of a reverting pixel without evidence of shared-copy cleanup or a contest over preservation.
Mascot discussion and an offer to restyle voting buttons bring the canvas figure into the room's continuing identity.
Repeated polls and a moderator's alternatives consider another canvas or a dog-posting future.
Future-purpose proposals must remain distinct from adoption when the moderator expresses uncertainty and surviving poll invitations reveal no result.
Mascot-making begins before shutdown, so retaining the effort overlaps active placing rather than requiring the event's completion first.
A member calls for fighting the Dutch, without that call alone proving coordinated placement.
A group demands anatomical changes and threatens to change the sign, making alteration of the artwork the object of a raid.
The contest continues through a refusal of compromise and an explicit promise to redouble the alteration effort.
A closing lament blames Dutch bots for unrealised small dogs despite separate expressions of alliance.
Recruitment and retrospective building reports lack a passage saying the call brought those builders to the canvas.
The retrospective starter account does not establish that those starters produced the surviving call for hands.
Creating and fixing are recalled together without evidence that a reported completed mark triggered upkeep as a distinct next stage.
A participant explicitly presents the clog design bargain as protection against Dutch destruction, supporting a reported connection between defence and negotiation.
Alliance is an explicit reason to leave neighbouring space alone, while the passage does not establish the settled-line mechanism itself.
Defence and automated placement coexist without evidence that manual capacity being overrun caused script adoption.
Retrospective construction and later celebration lack an explicit link from a report of completion to the celebration.
The goodbye receives a direct reply placing the dogs in history, supporting this local sequence without demonstrating archive-making as its causal effect.
Remembrance precedes future polls without a passage identifying the record of the work as what produced continuation plans.
A warning about bots and a later failed addition do not establish a judgement leading to relocation.
Design disputes and posted guides are visible without a concept establishing a template that settled a particular dispute in the unseen planning chat.
The coded bare assents accept negotiated proposals rather than demonstrably answering the recruitment call.
Help offers appear alongside defence without identifying a shortage of hands as the reason help was requested or sent.
A reply to permission sought for a neighbouring design both approves it and offers help, supporting a local permission-to-assistance connection.
The recruitment call and later fight call have no passage establishing that recruitment turned participants toward attacking.
The fight caller explicitly retracts the attack after a reply reports the agreed clog plan.
Correcting the caller's understanding of an existing design agreement precedes the explicit withdrawal of the attack call.
The attack call is answered by invoking the neighbours' existing agreement rather than proposing continued fighting.
The anatomical alteration demand continues into an explicit refusal of compromise and promised redoubled effort in a subsequent negotiation.
Joint design and ally language do not establish a common external threat causing the room to join a coalition.
The canvas-born room is confirmed without evidence of a prior host's recruitment flood causing a moderation boundary.
Conditional permission produces a question about room authority and an explicit reply disclaiming that authority.
